summary: Graeme MacQueen was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1974–1979) under Masatoshi Nagatomi, John B. Carman, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and served as a lecturer at McMaster University (~1977–2003).
Graham E. Clarke worked in the field of Tibetology. His academic posts included Senior Member at the University of Oxford and a position at the Institute of Development Studies.
Graham Lock works in the fields of Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied under teachers Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Priest specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied at the University of Cambridge (~1968–1971) and the London School of Economics (~1971–1974). His posts include Boyce Gibson Professor Emeritus at Melbourne (~2001) and Distinguished Professor at CUNY (~2009).

Graves Champney Haughton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the East India Company College (~1815–1817). He later served there as Professor (~1817–1827) and was secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1831–1832).

Gray Tuttle is a historian and Tibetologist who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard (~1995–2002) under William C. Kirby, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Philip A. Kuhn. He became an Associate Professor at Columbia University (~2005).

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli was an Italian scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1860 to 1907 and founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano.
Greg Bailey is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau. He held a professorship at La Trobe University from around 1978.
Gregor Ahn works in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit until around 1991 and became a professor at Heidelberg University in 2001.

Gregory Forgues works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a degree at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher and studied under Birgit Kellner as well as several traditional teachers.
Gregory Hillis is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at the University of Virginia in 1993 and later held an academic post at the same institution.

Gregory Max Seton specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UCSB, and the University of Oxford (D.Phil 2008–2015), where he was supervised by Vesna A. Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

Gregory P. A. Levine works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University before becoming an Associate Professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 1997.

Gregory Schopen is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Australian National University (~1975–1978) under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held professorships at Indiana University, UT Austin, and UCLA.

Grigorij Maksimovič Bongard-Levin specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Moscow State University under George Roerich and held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Moscow State University, and the Institute of World History.

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett. He has held positions at the University of Hong Kong and the University of British Columbia.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He held a research post at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1986–2004) and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.
Guankong was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a teacher at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China beginning in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1940–1946) and under Kodo Sawaki (~1940–1965). He held posts at the Ministry of the Treasury and Japan Securities Finance.

Gudrun Bühnemann is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Michael Hahn and Ernst Steinkellner at Bonn and Vienna. She held research posts in India and Japan before becoming a Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.
